title: The Significance of the Eternal Chess Game
next_chapter_hook: Mo Xiansheng gently placed a yellowed ancient scroll into Chen Ji's palm. The faded seal on the scroll's cover seemed to speak of a secret sealed away for ten thousand years.

text.content: Just as Chen Ji fell into shock, the protective Jade Pendant worn close to Su Qingyao's body suddenly burst forth with blinding white light, and a line of ancient text identical to that on the Fragment emerged slowly—it was a warning only Chen Ji could understand. His pupils contracted sharply, fingertips digging into his palm. Su Qingyao, seeing his face contorted in alarm, was about to ask what was wrong when Chen Ji abruptly raised his head, his gaze piercing through the night toward the direction of the Tianqing Sect Back Mountain Forbidden Grounds. There, a faint residual soul aura was quietly approaching.

The night wind rose suddenly, carrying the distinctive damp, musty scent of the Back Mountain. Chen Ji took a deep breath, turned to Su Qingyao and said softly, "Senior Sister Su, regarding tonight's events, you saw nothing." His voice was terrifyingly calm, as if stating an established fact. Su Qingyao frowned tightly, wanting to press further, but saw that Chen Ji had already stepped forward, heading toward the Back Mountain. His figure under the moonlight appeared exceptionally lonely, yet radiated a resolute determination to face death.

dialogue.content: "Since you've come, Mo Xiansheng, why hide and skulk?" Chen Ji's voice echoed across the empty Mountain Path, carrying a hint of mocking laughter. The Back Mountain was shrouded in mist, moonlight barely penetrating the layered ancient tree branches. His pace was unhurried, each step landing on precise positions, as if he had measured this path countless times before.

text.content: The moment his voice fell, a ghostly blue light slowly emerged from the depths of the mist. That light was like phosphorescence in the deep sea, flickering uncertainly yet carrying a certain eerie vitality. Following this, a illusory figure condensed into form—it was Mo Xiansheng. His form was even more translucent than their last meeting, nearly transparent, but those deep eyes still burned with unyielding fire. Mo Xiansheng gazed quietly at Chen Ji, a bitter smile appearing at the corner of his mouth.

dialogue.content: "You came faster than I anticipated." Mo Xiansheng's voice was low and hoarse, as if traversing endless years. He slowly raised his hand, translucent fingertips pointing toward the Tianji Record Fragment over Chen Ji's chest. "Those things you thought were my暗中 assistance—tonight, I should give you the truth." The mist churned around him, as if recreating that earth-shattering battle from ten thousand years ago.

text.content: Chen Ji said nothing, simply standing with hands clasped behind his back, his gazecalm地注视着这位mysterious的守护者。月光穿透墨先生虚淡的身躯，在地面投下一片破碎的光影。他见过太多disguised，太多谎言，在这乱世之中生存，怀疑是一切智慧的开始。但此刻，他心中却隐隐感到一丝异样的情绪——那是被蒙在鼓里的不甘。

dialogue.content: "Ten thousand years ago, I was the Fourth Chess Player." Mo Xiansheng's voice suddenly became incomparably heavy, like a bell ringing from antiquity. "At that time, the Tianji Record had four pages, belonging to four Chess Players. We joined hands to set up the Eternal Chess Game, attempting to break the Heavenly Dao's will that manipulated all living beings. However..." He paused, a deep-seated hatred flickering in his illusory eyes. "However, the Ultimate Chess Player betrayed us, sealing us one by one."

text.content: Chen Ji's pupils contracted slightly. Ultimate Chess Player—this term he had seen countless times in the Tianji Record Fragment, yet he never imagined such a terrifying truth lay behind it. He forced himself to remain composed, his mind racing through various possibilities. The night wind wailed, stirring his thin clothing, yet could not move half a wave of turmoil in his eyes. He was a vindictive person, and at this moment, this hatred was deeply buried within him, waiting for the right moment.

dialogue.content: "I should have completely dissipated into the heavens and earth." Mo Xiansheng gave a tragic smile, his illusory form trembling slightly. "It was the residual will of the Tianji Record's first page that condensed my remaining soul fragments until today. For ten thousand years, I have been waiting—waiting for someone who could break this chess game." He gazed at Chen Ji, his eyes burning with an almost madness-like obsession. "Do you know why I chose you?"

text.content: Chen Ji still did not speak. He disliked feeling manipulated, even if the other party's intentions were good. The night deepened, the Back Mountain's fog grew increasingly thick, as if to devour the entire world. He waited quietly, waiting for Mo Xiansheng to provide an answer. This silence was not cowardice, but acomposed掌控节奏的心态——他深谙人心，知道有时候沉默比追问更能让人吐露真相。

dialogue.content: "Because you are like me." Mo Xiansheng's voice suddenly became incomparably gentle, yet carried a bone-piercing sorrow. "We are both those chosen by the Tianji Record, yet abandoned by the Heavenly Dao. Every time you use your foresight ability, you are burning your own Heavenly Fate. And I..." He raised his illusory hand, gazing at those nearly transparent fingers. "Back then, to protect the legacy of the First Chess Player, I was sealed by the Ultimate Chess Player's own hands, even stripped of the qualification for reincarnation."

text.content: Chen Ji's Adam's apple rolled slightly. He remembered those moments of weakness after using the Tianji Record, remembered the terror of feeling emptied after every glimpse of the future. He had never mentioned these to anyone, because he knew—exposing weakness was the beginning of death. But at this moment, this Chess Player from ten thousand years ago had spoken his deepest fears. This feeling of being seen through filled him with anger and... an inexplicable sense of closeness.

dialogue.content: "My暗中 assistance was not to use you." Mo Xiansheng's voice trembled slightly, carrying an almost imperceptiblechoking up. "It's because... because watching you step by step reach where you are today, I see my past self. I don't want to watch another genius be crushed by this Eternal Chess Game." His illusory form fluctuated violently, as if about to dissipate into the wind at any moment. "I don't have much time left, Chen Ji. The truth of the Eternal Chess Game must be ended by you."

choice.prompt: After saying this, Mo Xiansheng's illusory gaze was full of anticipation and resolve. Chen Ji remained silent for a long while, the night wind stirring his hair, while complex emotions churned in his heart.

choices.description: "Since Heaven's way is unjust, then I shall overturn this chessboard." Chen Ji's voice was calm yet resolute. "The regrets of ten thousand years ago, tonight I shall make amends."

His voice trembled, carrying uncontrollable excitement. He slowly bowed deeply to Chen Ji, and the moment his illusory body bent, the surrounding mist actually stilled. "I speak on behalf of all those sacrificed by this chess game—thank you."

text.content: Mo Xiansheng showed no anger, instead revealing a bitter smile. "Your questioning is excellent." He said softly, "This is the temperament a true Chess Player should possess." He slowly raised his hand, a flash of light appearing, and a blurry image floated in the air—a scene of ten thousand years ago, with four silhouettes standing on either side of a chessboard, and on the chessboard's center, unmistakably carved the same mark as on Chen Ji's chest. "I have not deceived you, only some things, even if I told you, you would not believe."

text.content: Mo Xiansheng was stunned. He stared at Chen Ji, his surprise gradually transforming into appreciation. "Interesting..." A meaningful smile appeared at the corner of his mouth. "You are the first person to dare ask such a question. The Eternal Chess Game has existed for ten thousand years, and no one has ever questioned its rules—including me." He paced slowly, his illusory form flickering in and out of the fog. "Perhaps... this is precisely why you may succeed."

text.content: The night wind suddenly stopped. The entire Back Mountain fell into a诡异寂静, as if heaven and earth were both holding their breath, waiting for something. Mo Xiansheng's form grew increasingly translucent, yet the light in his eyes grew brighter and brighter. He raised his illusory hand, pointing toward the Tianji Record Fragment over Chen Ji's chest. There, a faint light was泛起微光, creating some kind of resonance with his remaining soul. "I don't have much time left, Chen Ji."

dialogue.content: "Whatever choice you make, I must tell you one final thing." Mo Xiansheng's voice became incomparably solemn, like an oath from ancient gods. "The Ultimate Chess Player has never disappeared—it has always been watching us from within the Heavenly Dao's will. Every time you use the Tianji Record, it will detect you." He gazed at Chen Ji, his eyes full of worry and reluctance. "The reason I have always approached you while hiding my aura was to buy you more time... but now, thethe right moment has arrived."

text.content: Chen Ji listened silently, yet in his heart, great waves were churning. The Ultimate Chess Player has never disappeared—this meant a sword always hung above his head, ready to fall at any moment. He remembered those blurry prophetic images in the Tianji Record Fragment, remembered the inexplicable palpitations after every glimpse of the future. So that wasn't an illusion, but the Heavenly Dao's will secretly observing. He slowly raised his head, his gaze穿透重重迷雾, gazing toward that unseen depths of the firmament.

dialogue.content: "Are you afraid?" Mo Xiansheng asked softly, his illusory eyes carrying a trace of heartache. "All along this road, you have endured too much. But I want to tell you—you are not alone. Even if I completely dissipate into the heavens and earth, my efforts, my lifetime of insights, will all remain within the Tianji Record." He extended his illusory hand, trembling as it attempted to touch Chen Ji's shoulder, yet stopped mid-air. "Remember, your life is your own."

text.content: Chen Ji gazed at that hand suspended in mid-air, and somewhere in his heart that was hard as stone, a crack silently formed. He thought of many things—those days of bearing everything alone, those secrets no one could tell, those choices he knew were dangerous yet had no choice but to make. He did have weaknesses; he simply hid them too deeply. But at this moment, this Chess Player from ten thousand years ago, with his remaining fragmented soul, told him: You are not alone. He took a deep breath, reached out his hand, and for the first time, proactively grasped that illusory hand.

Mo Xiansheng placed a yellowed ancient scroll gently into Chen Ji's palm. On that scroll's cover, a faded seal shimmered with faint light under the moonlight—the exact same aura as the Tianji Record Fragment. Chen Ji lowered his head, gazing at the scroll in his hands, and a indescribably heavy feeling surged in his heart. "The Eternal Chess Game..." he murmured softly. Mo Xiansheng smiled, his expression carryingrelieved与expectant. "Go, go write your own legend. This time, on the chessboard, there is only one Chess Player—and that is yourself."
